subject: Linguistics
title: Fusional Languages
description: A short lesson to help you apply Fusional Languages.

hook.text: Spanish 'hablo' means 'I speak'—the ending '-o' marks first person, singular, and present all at once.

buildup.text: Fusional languages pack multiple grammatical meanings into a single, inseparable morpheme.

discovery.text: Latin, Russian, and Arabic are heavily fusional—one ending does the work of several.

twist.text: This makes fusional forms harder to segment than agglutinative ones—the meanings are tangled.

climax.text: Old English was fusional; modern English shed most of its fusions, moving toward isolation.

punchline.text: One ending, many meanings, all fused together.

quiz.question: How do fusional languages differ from agglutinative ones?
options: One morpheme carries multiple meanings at once
